After using the app for a while, every prompt send fails with a "Failed to fetch" toast; restarting the app is the only recovery. The sidecar itself appears to stay alive (the core process keeps logging to `log/opencode.log` normally the whole time).

The server-side log shows repeated transient network failures around daily usage, which I suspect are what trigger the renderer-side `ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED` disconnect described above:

```
level=ERROR message="Failed to fetch models.dev" cause="... GET https://models.opencode.ai/api.json ... getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND models.opencode.ai"
level=ERROR message="stream error" ... error.error="AI_APICallError: Cannot connect to API: read ECONNRESET"
level=ERROR message=process ... error=Aborted stack="AbortError: Aborted ..."
```

These recurred across multiple days (Sep 2/3/4/7/8/10) on this machine (fluctuating network: Wi-Fi + VPN/proxy). After each such event the renderer never reconnects to the local sidecar, so all UI requests fail with `TypeError: Failed to fetch` until restart.

Would love a renderer-side auto-reconnect (or automatic reload) when fetches to `127.0.0.1` start failing, instead of requiring a full app restart.

## Update: Root Cause Analysis

The original hypothesis (database size >2GB) was incorrect. After extensive investigation:

### Crash Signature (consistent across 30+ crashes)
- **Binary offset**: `0x1CDA3D8` (same in every crash)
- **Instruction**: `brk #0xc471` (deliberate assertion failure)
- **Source**: WebKit `vendor/WebKit/Source/WTF/wtf/text/StringImpl.h` line 894
- **Assertion**: `RELEASE_ASSERT(m_length <= MaxLength)` where `MaxLength = int32_t::max()` (2GB)
- **ESR**: `0xF200C471` (macOS misreports as "pointer authentication trap IB")
- **Thread**: Worker (JSC GC/JS execution)

### What Was Tried (all failed)
1. Database cleanup (1.8GB → 501MB) — still crashes
2. Session reduction (898 → 50) — still crashes
3. Delete large events (>10KB) — still crashes
4. Disable auto compaction — still crashes
5. Remove DCP plugin — still crashes
6. Upgrade Bun 1.4.0 → 1.4.2 — still crashes

### Key Finding
The crash happens **after every session completes** (when saving/serializing session state). The database is only 501MB with max session at 10MB — nowhere near the 2GB limit.

This suggests opencode is serializing session state into a single string that exceeds 2GB during the save/compaction process, even though the stored data is small.

### Reproduction
1. Start opencode session
2. Have a normal conversation (even short)
3. When session completes/saves → crash with `trace trap`

### Environment
- opencode 1.18.30
- Bun 1.4.2 (also tested 1.4.0)
- macOS 26.0, Apple M3 Pro (arm64)

### Request
Please investigate the session serialization/save path. The bug is likely in how opencode accumulates or serializes session state, not in Bun itself.

Been poking at reconnect behavior lately (see #48161 on v2 — client-side backoff, different layer, so no overlap here), so I read through this diff.

Main thing: the `consecutiveErrors = 0` at the top of the for-await means a server that accepts the stream, emits a single event and then dies gets the full 250ms base delay again on every cycle, forever. That flapping pattern is basically where backoff earns its keep, so maybe reset the counter only after the stream has stayed healthy for a bit (say N seconds of events) instead of on first event.

Nit: with the 5s cap, the exponent clamp `Math.min(consecutiveErrors, 8)` can't actually engage at this base — 250ms x 1.5^7 is ~4.3s and anything beyond that hits the cap anyway, so the clamp is dead code unless the base ever drops under ~200ms.

#48014 looks assigned internally, so if this overlaps with planned work no worries — leaving notes in case they're useful.

## Critical Update: Root Cause Identified

### Crash Trigger
Crash happens **after a long session completes, when sending new content**.

### Evidence
- Database size: 136MB total, 3MB for crashing session (NOT the issue)
- All plugins disabled, compaction disabled — still crashes
- Bun upgraded 1.4.0 → 1.4.2 — still crashes
- Crash offset: `0x1CDA3D8` (WebKit `StringImpl.h:894`)

### Root Cause Hypothesis

**Runtime memory accumulation, not database size.**

1. **Unbounded PubSub**: `PubSub.unbounded<Payload>()` in `packages/core/src/event.ts:155` creates unbounded channel
2. **Dense event publishing**: Every text fragment, tool call, reasoning step publishes events
3. **Memory accumulation**: Events accumulate in memory during long sessions
4. **Serialization overflow**: When serializing accumulated events (for LLM context or persistence), creates string >2GB
5. **WebKit assertion**: `RELEASE_ASSERT(m_length <= MaxLength)` fails

### Reproduction
1. Start opencode session
2. Have a long conversation with大量 tool outputs (data analysis, file reads, etc.)
3. Session completes
4. Send new message → **crash with SIGTRAP**

### Code Location
- `packages/core/src/event.ts:155` — `PubSub.unbounded<Payload>()`
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts` — dense event publishing
- `packages/core/src/session/runner/to-llm-message.ts` — serialization to LLM context

### Suggested Fix
1. Add backpressure to event system (bounded PubSub or throttling)
2. Limit in-memory event accumulation
3. Stream event serialization instead of building single string
4. Add memory usage monitoring and warning

### Workaround
- Avoid very long sessions with大量 tool outputs
- Restart opencode frequently
- Monitor memory usage

Thanks @nolanderc, this was exactly the cause in my environment.

I had `/home/ubuntu/.local/share/opencode` mounted into an Ubuntu 24.04 devcontainer. Docker created the missing parent `/home/ubuntu/.local/share` as `root:root`, so OpenCode could not create `/home/ubuntu/.local/share/opentui/tree-sitter`. Correcting only the parent ownership restored Markdown rendering:

```bash
sudo install -d -m 0755 -o ubuntu -g ubuntu \
  /home/ubuntu/.local \
  /home/ubuntu/.local/share
```

For a durable container fix, I now create those parent directories with the correct owner during the image build and repair only those exact paths during startup. The OpenCode bind mount and its contents remain untouched.

For a general upstream solution, OpenCode/OpenTUI could surface the tree-sitter storage error and keep a Markdown fallback when the OpenTUI data directory is unavailable. The current silent fallback to raw Markdown makes this filesystem problem very difficult to diagnose.

## Update: opencode 1.18.30 embeds Bun 1.3.14

The opencode binary at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` is a self-contained executable with an embedded Bun runtime. Running `strings` on it reveals:

```
bun-v1.3.14
```

**opencode 1.18.30 is compiled with Bun 1.3.14**, not 1.4.x.

The crash is in Bun's embedded WebKit (`StringImpl.h:894`), so this is a **Bun-level bug**, not opencode code.

### Bun issue filed
https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/42268

### Workaround
No known workaround yet. The bug affects Bun 1.3.14 on M3 Pro. Possible fixes:
1. Bun releases a patched version with updated WebKit
2. opencode recompiles with a newer Bun version that has the fix
3. User switches to a non-M3-Pro machine

The comparator here used to be a 15 byte stub that called Effect's `Equal.equals`. It is now a 359 byte function that checks each of the nine row types directly.

```text
before: load "equals", call it       15 bytes
after:  switch on "_tag", compare   359 bytes
```

The group check is shared with `session-ui`, and the diff rows still use `Equal.equals`.

Numbers from the benchmark, which runs the real modules over a 1,288 row timeline:

- 1,000 updates per run, medians of 5: 11.5 ms per update before, 0.64 ms after. That is a 94% drop.
- Running the same build against itself moved less than 2%, so the gap is not noise.
- Browser run, production build, 30x CPU throttle: script time 73.0 s to 35.7 s, longest task 1.73 s to 0.36 s, total long tasks 88.9 s to 49.9 s. Text, rows, parts, and scroll position were unchanged.
- 726 unit tests pass, including a new test that compares this function with `Equal.equals` for every row type. It runs on every PR. 43 perf tests pass.

Why this path matters: the timeline rebuilds its row list in a memo whenever messages or parts change, so every streamed update compares the whole timeline with the previous one. The fixture does 1,288 comparisons per update. Before, Effect's equal/hash code held 34.4% of JS samples; after, none.

I tested fixing Effect instead. Skipping the hash check inside `compareObjects` changed a one-off benchmark by about 3%, so the expensive part is the generic walk itself. A function that knows the row types skips it without touching Effect.

Each build runs in its own process. When two builds share one process, the engine's optimizations for one can distort the other's numbers.

An AI agent wrote this change while following a documented process. I reproduced the benchmark and tests myself; the browser numbers come from the agent's run.

Draft PR with the measured fix: #48435.

Summary of what is verified: the comparator agrees with `Equal.equals` for every row variant pair as a unit test in the normal CI suite, the isolated reconcile A/B reproduces at 11,527 us to 642 us per reconcile (-94.4%, A/A within 1.7%), and the browser run shows script time and long tasks roughly halved with identical rendered output. Full bytecode and counter evidence is in the PR comment.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #36985: Same root cause — shell tool and PowerShell on Windows needing UTF-8 console encoding; even describes the same workaround (setting `[Console]::OutputEncoding`)
- #23636: PowerShell output encoding for non-ASCII characters on Windows
- #37915: Garbled output in PowerShell on non-English Windows (encoding mismatch)
- #47350: Shell tool never returns when a command leaves a background process holding its stdio (similar hang symptom)

If your issue is specifically about the hang/deadlock due to mid-sequence UTF-8 bytes (rather than just garbled output), it may still warrant a separate report — but please review the above and comment on whether any of them already cover your scenario.

Reviewed all four. #36985 / #23636 / #37915 describe **mojibake only** — the output comes back garbled. My report is different: **no output is returned at all — the tool hangs**, even though the command completed (verified on disk afterwards). Same root cause (stdout decoded as UTF-8 while pwsh emits the legacy code page), but the *hang* is an undocumented consequence of it.

Closest symptom is #47350, but its mechanism differs — there a background child holds stdio open so EOF never arrives. Here it's a short one-shot `Get-ChildItem`/`Rename-Item` pipeline with no child process; the stream simply never completes, consistent with the reader blocking on a **partial UTF-8 multibyte sequence** at end-of-output.

So: root cause = #36985, hang mechanism = related to #47350, but the combination (encoding -> hang) isn't covered by either. Happy to consolidate into #36985 if maintainers prefer, but I think the hang is worth its own tracking.

Root cause identified — not an opencode core or database issue.

A third-party telemetry plugin (opencode-agenttrack, installed via the AIWorkKit oc-cc dogfooding setup) hooks every LLM call and appends the full request/response body to `~/.cache/opentelemetry.instrumentation.opencode/sessions/proxy_events_<uuid>.jsonl` with no rotation or size cap. Growth is quadratic in session length (every request re-sends the full history); a rate-limit retry storm grew one file to 2,495,795,160 bytes on 2026-09-10 15:57:26. The same plugin's turn-end report then runs `readFileSync(file, "utf-8")` on every file in that global directory. Constructing a JS string longer than INT32_MAX UTF-16 units trips Bun's embedded WTF `RELEASE_ASSERT(data.size() <= MaxLength)` (StringImpl.h:894) → `brk #0xc471` → SIGTRAP. The plugin's try/catch cannot catch it (native assert, not a JS exception).

This explains every symptom: first crash 29 s after the file crossed the threshold; all 43 crashes byte-identical; every session/project crashed 20–90 s after a turn completed (global file re-read at turn end); database (540 MB, 3.4 MB max row) was never the trigger.

Corrections to earlier comments in this issue: not hardware-specific; ESR 0xF200C471 is a BRK exception (macOS's "pointer authentication trap IB" label is misleading); unrelated to #38362/#41175/#43551/#47854. Same mechanism as #46535.

Workaround: quarantine/delete files >2 GB in that directory, or uninstall the plugin. The plugin needs a size cap/rotation and streaming reads to prevent recurrence.

Ran the step-4 passthrough capture against a different Anthropic-protocol gateway. The result cuts against the "custom providers never get marks" framing: **opencode does put `cache_control` on the wire for a custom `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider, and the upstream honors it.**

Setup: opencode 1.18.30, `llm.runtime=ai-sdk`, custom provider with `npm: "@ai-sdk/anthropic"` + custom `baseURL`, bare native-style model ids (no `anthropic/` prefix). Logging passthrough on localhost, `baseURL` pointed at it via `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, request bodies parsed per call.

Three runs (plain-text tool result; image `read`; a stub MCP server returning text + image + text). Every captured `/v1/messages` body carried the mark:

```json
{"tool_result_cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"},
 "inner_types": "str",
 "inner_cache_control": null}
```

And a hand-rolled call to the same gateway with an explicit mark returns `cache_creation_input_tokens: 651`, so that route honors marks.

Two things this pins down for @utadamaaya's case:

1. The `useMessageLevelOptions` check at `transform.ts:384-388` gates on `model.providerID === "anthropic"` (exact string), so a custom provider name does take the `shouldUseContentOptions` branch. But as @seven7763 said, that only relocates where the mark sits — it does not remove it. My capture can't distinguish the two branches (a tool message with a single `tool_result` receives the mark in the same place either way), but it does show the mark reaching the wire on the custom-provider path.
2. Because marks do reach the wire here, `cache_creation = 0` in the original report points at the proxy route rather than a missing transform — consistent with suspect #3, the `anthropic/`-prefixed model id.

@utadamaaya — the passthrough capture is cheap and decisive. If your body shows `cache_control`, the report belongs with OfoxAI, not here.

Correction to my comment above — one of my two supporting data points was wrong, and the retraction actually sharpens the conclusion.

I wrote that a hand-rolled call to that gateway with an explicit mark returned `cache_creation_input_tokens: 651`, "so that route honors marks." That inference does not hold. I re-ran it as a controlled three-variant test (independent nonces so no variant reads another's cache, same model, non-streaming):

| variant | client `cache_control` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| legal | on `tool_result` | 200, `cache_creation_input_tokens: 13970` (`ephemeral_1h`) |
| illegal | inside `tool_result.content[1]` | 200, `cache_creation_input_tokens: 13997` (`ephemeral_1h`) |
| **none** | **no `cache_control` anywhere** | **200, `cache_creation_input_tokens: 13977` (`ephemeral_1h`)** |

The `none` row settles it: a payload with zero marks still produced ~14k tokens of cache creation. Anthropic does not create cache without a breakpoint, so the gateway is inserting its own. Corroborating detail — all three landed in the `ephemeral_1h` bucket, though the client never requested a 1h TTL (that needs an explicit `ttl` plus the beta header). The gateway is choosing the TTL too.

So the pipeline on that route is: **client `cache_control` discarded → gateway injects its own → upstream.** The 651 figure measured the gateway's breakpoint, not mine.

What still stands: the passthrough capture showing opencode emits `cache_control` on the wire for a custom `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider. That was measured before the request left the machine, so it is unaffected.

What this changes for @utadamaaya: an Anthropic-protocol proxy can rewrite caching wholesale, in either direction. Mine adds breakpoints that were never sent; one that drops them and does not re-add would produce exactly your symptom — `cache_creation = 0` forever, no matter what opencode emits. Proxy-side usage numbers therefore cannot be used to infer whether the client sent marks; only a capture taken **before** the proxy can. That makes the step-4 passthrough capture the only measurement worth acting on here.

Apologies for the noise — better to correct it than leave it pointing the wrong way.

Thanks, and good catch on the small model — you're right, and it does change part of the fix.

## On the frozen-account models

I checked the selection against the June 2026 freeze and your reading is exactly right. v2's `Catalog.model.small` walks a single global priority list (`packages/core/src/catalog.ts:226`):

```
["gpt-luna", "gemini-flash-lite", "gemini-flash", "claude-haiku"]
```

On your account the first two are unusable — `gpt-5.6-luna` is 2026-07-09 and there is no flash-lite at all — so it falls through to `gemini-3.5-flash`. Meanwhile v1 had a Copilot branch here: `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:1974` used `["gpt-mini", ...smallModelFamilyPriority]`, plus the `UTILITY_MODELS` override in the plugin (`gpt-5.4-nano`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`). On a frozen account that resolves to `gpt-5.4-mini`. So v2 dropped Copilot's provider-specific priority and your account lands on a different small model than v1 did.

To be precise about what that does and does not explain: on a per-request plan every one of those models costs the same 1 request, so the model choice is not what drained your quota. It is still a real part of the fix though — I'll restore the Copilot-specific priority along with the header change, otherwise the small-model behaviour stays wrong on frozen accounts even after the billing is fixed.

## The part that actually drained it

v1 classified the request itself. `packages/opencode/src/plugin/github-copilot/copilot.ts:366` set `X-Interaction-Type: agent-session-name-generation` for `incoming.agent === "title"` — that string no longer exists anywhere in v2, and `interactionType` now only emits `conversation-agent` / `conversation-background` / `conversation-compaction` / `conversation-subagent`. So a request kind that v1 sent as a utility interaction is now sent as one that bills against your quota.

## Your alert idea

That one is separate and I think worth doing on its own, because right now you would get no warning at all. The only quota-exhausted UI is `GO_UPSELL_PROVIDERS = new Set(["opencode", "opencode-go"])` in `packages/app/src/session/usage-exceeded-dialogs.tsx:16`, and nothing in the session UI references `github-copilot`. So Copilot users get no signal before the quota is gone.

## What would help from your side

If you can still reach their API, the one thing I cannot determine from the source is whether attempts that were already rejected with 429 also count against the quota. In v2 a `RateLimit` failure is retryable and bounded by `Schedule.max([exponential 2s, recurs(4)])` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/retry.ts`), so every step can emit up to ~5 extra requests after you are already out. If a `Retry-After` or remaining-quota header comes back on that 429, that would settle it. If requests are only counted on success, then the classification change above is the whole story and the retry behaviour is harmless.

I'll open a PR for the classification restore plus the Copilot-specific small-model priority, and keep the alert as a follow-up so it stays reviewable.
